column9: Ukrainian negation, inflected
25yo peated expression.
Intensely Peated NAS expression.
officially branded 'Blackpitts Peated Single Malt' on teelingwhiskey.com; exact ppm not stated, heavy is a judgment call given it is marketed as the house's dedicated peated expression
Confirmed peated to about 25ppm.

Wikipedia: 'the Dragon range comprising Legend (Madeira finish), Myth (Bourbon finish) and Celt (Peated)' -- Celt is Penderyn's peated Dragon-range expression; Legend/Myth are not peated so no rule needed for them.
10yo peated expression (heavily peated malt).
Described as mildly peated, lighter than Bold.
'Fortnight' is a heavily peated (54ppm) once-a-year release, distinct from the unpeated core Stobcross/Napier range.
Spey Fumare (2016) was explicitly 'the first ever peated whisky from the Speyside distillery'; core range stays none.
25% peated Scottish malt / 75% unpeated Indian malt; described as "gentle peat presence"

Distillery's own product page: 'A departure from our typically lightly peated single malt, our Heavily Peated Kilkerran is released twice per year at cask strength and around 45PPM.' Supersedes out/08/rule.tsv's same-pattern row, which had no citation.
2013 limited series explicitly named 'Heavily Peated', distinct from the core range (see producer.tsv note, peatProfile=light there)

Clan Denny Islay blended malt vats Ardbeg, Bowmore, Bruichladdich, Bunnahabhain, Caol Ila and 2 undisclosed Islay distilleries - described as having phenolic/smoked character. Highland and Speyside editions are NOT covered by this rule and fall back to the producer row's own unpeated baseline.
Arran's peated expression line (first released 8 Dec 2010 per Wikipedia); core Arran is unpeated. No specific ppm source found, recorded as medium.

Bunnahabhain's core range is unpeated but its Mòine range is heavily peated. This exact pairing is stated in this research task's own brief as a known sibling case; not independently re-verified via an opened source, so sourceUrls is left empty per the "never invent a citation" rule even though the note is confident.
Morven is Wolfburn's one peated expression ("a delicate touch of peat"); the rest of the core range including this batch's sample Langskip is unpeated (see producer row).
Permanent no-age-statement expression named simply 'Peat', introduced 2016; treated as heavy given the Islay peated-malt convention.
Hyde No. 11 The Peat Cask and similar releases are heavily peated; base range otherwise mixed/unpeated. Pattern may not catch every peated release name in the full 23-product catalogue.
Dedicated "Bavarian PEAT" expression; core range is unpeated.
Covers "Peat Week" / "Week of Peat" release names.

Marketed/named as a fully peated blended malt; not observed in this batch's samples (Hedonism, Nectarosity, Artist Blend, Crimson Cask, Glasgow Blend, Orchard House) but added defensively since it is a well-known Compass Box line
100% Finnish rye malt smoked 24h with Finnish freshwater peat in a traditional Riihi barn
Matches brief's own worked example verbatim: distinct heavily-peated bottling alongside the lightly-peated core range.
~23-24ppm phenol - moderate/mid-range peat, comparable to Bowmore rather than Islay's heaviest
Explicit "Speyside Single Malt Scotch Whisky Peated" bottling under this range; base range peat level otherwise unknown
Explicit 'Peated Single Malt' release, described as gentle/delicate smokiness rather than an extreme Islay-style peating - medium rather than heavy.
Peated Select Cask line uses imported Islay and Aberdeen peat, distinct from the unpeated core range (Brilliance/Edited/Nirvana/Classic)
21 Year Old The Peated Blend incorporates peated malts; described as adding "subtle smokiness", not extreme.
Peated Finish is red-wine-cask spirit finished about 18 months in peated Islay casks; rated medium since it is a cask finish rather than primary peated-malt maturation.
The Peated NAS expression; specific ppm not published so rated medium.
Peated Reserve variant exists; intensity not detailed so rated medium conservatively.
Distillery also produces "Peated English Malt" / "Peated Black Malt" spirit; ppm not published so rated medium. Exact bottling name carrying "Peated" not confirmed.

Togouchi Peated Cask Finish: bourbon-cask matured then finished in ex-Islay casks, non-chill-filtered, explicitly smoky/peaty on the mid-palate; exact ppm not published so kept medium rather than heavy.
Separate 'Evade Peated' / 'Evade Peated Wine Cask Finish' single malt expression exists alongside the unpeated base and other cask finishes; exact ppm not published.
Third member of the Signature Range alongside The Original and Triple Distilled, described as 'rich and smoky'; exact ppm not published so kept medium.
Explicit NAS "Peated" expression (Oloroso sherry casks, 54%+ ABV per Wikipedia); core GlenDronach is unpeated. No specific ppm/intensity source found, so recorded as medium rather than heavy.

Glendalough Pot Still Peated is an explicit peated expression (Gold Global Irish Whiskey Masters per their site); the core range (Double Barrel, single malt, single grain) is unpeated. No specific intensity source found, recorded as medium.

No citation opened for this specific release this session (see producer note); rule written directly from this batch's own sample product name ("Westland Peated"). Exact intensity not independently confirmed -- a reviewer may want to downgrade to medium.

Matches this batch's own sample "Glenturret Peated" and existing precedent in this project's batch 07 rule.tsv. See the producer row's note for the fuller, genuinely complicated peat history (traditional peat-smoke kilning, a "Peat Smoked" range, and a Nov-2024 announcement to remove peat from 2025) that this rule is deliberately not trying to resolve at the producer-default level.
Covers "Peated Triple Cask" release name.
Peaty Collection / Peated Edition releases, ~20ppm; matches this batch's own sample "AnCnoc Sherry Peated".
Elements Peated Cask edition; smokiness is cask-derived from ex-Islay casks rather than peated malt, but is consistently reviewed and marketed as a peated dram.

Hinch's own site lists a "Peated Single Malt" and "Peated Small Batch" alongside its unpeated core range. Exact ppm/phenol level not found; medium is an estimate based on the typical style of Irish peated single malt (cf. Connemara) rather than Islay-heavy peating, so treat with caution.

Sample "Black Bull Peated Finish" implies a peat-finished variant distinct from the unpeated core blend. The cited source confirms the company/brand only, not the specific peat level — medium is an unverified estimate for a cask-finish treatment rather than a fully peated malt; flagged for reviewer.

'Glen Moray Classic Peated' launched 2015 per scotchwhisky.com whiskypedia; exact ppm/intensity not stated there, medium is an estimate (not Islay-extreme, marketed as an accessible classic-peated style).
Wikipedia infobox lists 'Penderyn Peated' (Single Malt, cask: Bourbon, Peated) as one of the three core brand expressions; intensity not ppm-stated, medium is an estimate.
This batch's only sample, "Glen Clan Smoky Peated Blend", states both descriptors directly in the product name -- treated as heavy given the explicit double emphasis ("Smoky" and "Peated" together).

Evidenced directly by this batch's own product name ('Prologue Peated Small Batch No.2'), not an external source -- no citable URL found for the Prologue brand itself. Kept at medium (clearly peated but intensity unconfirmed) rather than heavy.
Peatist Series uses lightly peated malt sourced from Europe.
Solist Peaty Cask uses lightly peated malt.
Distillery bottles a distinct "Peaty Tang" expression alongside its unpeated core range.
35ppm phenol special edition, well above the light core range; not observed in this batch's samples (all bare 'Jura') but added defensively
Peated to ~5ppm - Teerenpeli's dedicated "smoke" single malt. Not itself present in this batch's samples, added defensively for future catalogue entries
17yo peated expression.
Wikipedia: 'Smokey Monkey Batch 9, a blend that includes Islay whiskies' - medium rather than heavy since Islay malt is blended with the usual unpeated Speyside malts, not the whole content
The Famous Grouse Smoky Black (renamed from "The Black Grouse" in 2015) is a peated variant; the core Famous Grouse blend is unpeated.
Distillery's unpeated-core range carries a separately named peated line (The Smoky Ten / The Smoky Twelve); matches the brief's own worked example.
Grant's Triple Wood Smoky variant is described as finishing with smoke (cask-derived, non-peat); core range and this row's peatProfile stay "none".
Catalogue sample 'Glen Moray Smoky' is presumed to be the same Peated expression under an alternate market name; same intensity estimate as the Peated rule.

Sir Edward's own site lists a distinct 'Smoky' variant in its range alongside Finest/Beer Reserve/Aged 12 Years. Not in this batch's samples (which are 'Finest', the base unpeated blend) but recorded so a future Smoky bottling does not inherit Finest's unpeated profile. Exact ppm/intensity not stated, kept at medium rather than heavy.
~70% peated malt; Mackmyra's dedicated smoky release, distinct from the (assumed) unpeated core range. Not itself present in this batch's samples, added defensively for future catalogue entries
Barley peated to 30ppm for the Tourbe (Tourbe) collection; pattern written unaccented, matching layer folds accents.

Tourbe = French for peat; distillery site lists a "Peated" expression (URL slug "troube") as a distinct product from "Original". Exact ppm/intensity not confirmed - medium is a conservative estimate, flagged for reviewer.

Wiki: "Since 1999, the distillery has also produced a non-peated 'highland spirit'", occasionally released as Diageo Special Releases labelled "Unpeated"; the core range is peated (medium, see producer row).
Alder-wood smoked, explicitly NOT peat - "flavour doesn't come from traditional peating"
